'''Peter Chadwick''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRS}} (23 March 1931 – 12 August 2018) was a British applied mathematician and physicist.

A [[Huddersfield]] native born on 23 March 1931, Chadwick attended the [[University of Manchester]] (BSc, 1952) and completed his PhD at [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]] in 1957. He was Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of East Anglia]] from 1965 to 1991, and was made a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ogden|first=R. W.|date=2020|title=Peter Chadwick. 23 March 1931—12 August 2018|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2020.0012|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=69|pages=109–131 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0012 |s2cid=219181693 |doi-access=free}}</ref> in 1977. He died on 12 August 2018, aged 87.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Norton |first1=Joseph |title=Former head of UEA school known for immaculate writing dies |url=http://www.edp24.co.uk/news/obituaries/peter-chadwick-obit-1-5659812 |access-date=26 August 2018 |work=Eastern Daily Press |date=20 August 2018}}</ref>
